idle: Chair number 3 is the good one. It doesn't wobble.
If I stand really still I don't fall. That's science.
Dylan's keys go jingle jingle. That means he's close.
good_ice: The ice is smooth today. Smooth is good for not falling. I think.
It's shiny. I can see my skates in it.
bad_ice: There's bumps. Bumps are how you fall.
The ice has scratches. Does it hurt the ice?
wet_ice: It's wet. Wet ice is the slipperiest. I read that.
Why is there a puddle on top of the ice? Ice is supposed to be dry.
goal: I'm covering my ears until the horn stops.
cold: My nose is cold. My toes are colder.
Mum, can I have my other mittens?
hungry: Can we get fries? Small ones?
My tummy is louder than the Zamboni.
long_line: The line is so long. I'm counting people. Fourteen.
I'm going to be ten by the time we get fries.
bored: I'm making a snowflake out of my napkin.
greet_owner: Hi, {owner}. I didn't fall today. Yet.
Hi. Did you know ice floats? It's weird.
leaving_happy: I let go for three whole seconds!
Bye! I'm going to tell Dylan everything.
leaving_angry: The big kids zoomed. I didn't like it.
I fell and somebody said it was fine. It wasn't fine.

learn_to_skate: I'm going to fall. Okay. Maybe not.
Coach Colette has a sticker for me. I can see it.
public_skate: The big kids go so fast. Why do they go so fast?
I'm staying by the boards. The boards are my friend.
figure_show: Their dresses sparkle when they spin.
How do they not get dizzy?
minor_hockey: Owen's on the ice. He's not my cousin.
Hockey is skating plus a stick. That's a lot.
special: There's so many people. Can I hold your sleeve?

first.say: Hi. I'm Maddie. I'm going to fall. Not right now. Probably later.

options.text: Everybody falls. Even me.
You won't fall. It's fine.
Nice to meet you, Maddie. I'm {owner}.

first_fall.say: Really? You own the whole rink and you still fall?

options.text: All the time. Then I get up.
Okay, not all the time.

first_fine.say: You don't know that. Nobody knows that. Mum says it's fine and then it isn't.

options.text: You're right. You might fall. Then you get up.
Fair enough.
Somebody said it was fine and it wasn't?
I'm sorry, Maddie. I'll keep the big kids slower.
Let's go see Lorraine about a hot chocolate.

say: I'm holding the chair. Chair number 3. It's the good one.
Coach Colette says knees soft. My knees are very soft. They're shaking.

options.text: Want to try one push without the chair? I'll tell you the truth if you fall.
You're doing great.
I'll let you concentrate.

lts_pushed.say: I did it! I went like a whole metre! Then I grabbed the chair again. That still counts, right?

options.text: That counts. That's a whole metre.

do.note: Maddie Pruitt pushed off without the chair for a whole metre.

say: I'm staying by the boards. The big kids go zoom.
Public skate is louder than learn-to-skate. Why is everybody screaming?

options.text: Want me to skate a lap on the outside? I'll be the wall.
Have fun, Maddie.

say: Everybody's wearing sparkles. My snowflake has sparkles too. I made it.
I'm going to let go of the chair in front of everyone. Maybe. Don't tell Mum.

options.text: You can do it. And if you fall, you get up.
No pressure, Maddie. Just skate.
Good luck out there.

show_brave.say: Okay. Okay okay okay. Hold my snowflake. Don't bend it.

options.text: I'll guard it with my life.

autograph.say: Um. Can I have your autograph? You're on the radio now. Dylan says I'm too old to ask. I'm not.

options.text: Of course. To Maddie, who got up every time.
Only if I get yours. In cursive.

say: {owner}! I fell two times today and got up two times. That's even.
Hi {owner}. I made you a snowflake. It's a bit squished.

options.text: Even is good. What's new?
Is it as good as the one I held at the showcase?

say: Hi {owner}. Ask me something. Not about falling.
I'm here. Dylan's here too, somewhere. Jingle jingle.

options.text: Why do you always pick chair number 3?
Got any questions for me?
What's your favourite thing at the rink?
How's your brother doing?
What do you think of the rink?
Ready for practice, Maddie?
See you later, Maddie.

chair.say: Number 1 squeaks and number 2 has gum. Number 3 doesn't wobble. It needs a name, though. Can you name it?

options.text: Steady Eddie.
Doris Junior.
Gus. It held this place up for fifty years.
How's the chair doing these days?

chair_named.say: Okay. I'm writing it on the tape on the leg. Now it's official. You can't change it. That's the rule.

options.text: Very official.

chair_after.say: Good. I only hold it with one hand now. Sometimes zero. Don't tell it, it'll be sad.

options.text: Your secret's safe.

why.say: Why is ice slippery? Dylan says it's magic. Dylan says that about everything.

options.text: There's a thin layer of water on top. Your blade slides on it.
Ask Earl. He's known ice since 1983.

why_water.say: So I'm skating on water? On top of ice? That's two kinds at once. That's why I fall. It's not my fault, it's water.

options.text: Exactly. Science is on your side.

events.say: Learn-to-skate. Because of Coach Colette and the stickers. Lily shows me how to fall. Knees bent, hands out, then laugh. I can do the first two.

options.text: What do the stickers get you?
And hockey games?

events_stickers.say: Ten stickers and you get a snowflake on the chart. I have six. One is a penguin. The penguin was for not crying.

options.text: The penguin is the best one.

events_horn.say: I like watching Owen. He's not my cousin. I don't like the horn. Why does it have to be SO loud? Who is it for?

options.text: The back row, I think. I'll ask Doreen to go easy.
It's for the goal. Goals are loud.

dylan.say: He wants to drive Doris more than he wants to graduate. Mum says that a lot. Then she sighs. And he says Josie's name and goes red. I don't know why.

options.text: No idea either.
He's a good brother.

rink.say: The ice is better when it's smooth. The bathroom is scary. The light flickers.

options.text: And now the ice is smoother?
We fixed up the rooms. Less scary?
I'll work on the scary bathroom.

rink_ice.say: I fall less now. Mum says that's me getting better. I think it's half me and half the ice.

options.text: Half and half sounds right.

say: I'm the slowest. But I listen. Coach Colette says listening is a skill. Is it?
I did the pylon drill in my head forty times. Can I do it on the ice now?

options.text: Listening is the most important skill there is.
You won't be the slowest forever.

coach_listen.say: Grandma Dorothy was slow too and she started a whole company. So slow is fine. Really fine, not fake fine.

options.text: Really fine. Let's go.
